subject: Agriculture
title: The Shrinking Farm Workforce
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Shrinking Farm Workforce.

hook.text: In 1900, 40% of Americans worked on farms. Today it's under 2%. The food output is vastly larger.

buildup.text: Machines, chemicals, and better seeds replaced human labor at every stage of farming.

discovery.text: One American farmer today feeds about 166 people. In 1900, one farmer fed just seven.

twist.text: Rural communities shrank as farming needed fewer hands. Schools, shops, and hospitals closed.

climax.text: Productivity soared, but the human cost was rural depopulation across every industrialized nation.

punchline.text: Farming feeds more with fewer—and empties the countryside.

quiz.question: How many people does one American farmer feed today?
